Labour can be divided into 3 stages:

**Stage 1:**

- Onset of uterine contractions → cervical effacement 
- Latent \<4cm cervical dilation 
- Active \>4cm Cervical dilatation to fully dilated 

**Pain mechanism** 

- Visceral Pain caused by visceral stretch of uterus and cervix 
- Escalating poorly localised pain 

**Pain Pathways**

- nociceptors in the lower uterine segment and cervix transmit through afferent pain fibres predominantly C fibres (also A Δ) travel via the  sympathetic efferent nerve supply → inferior hypogastric plexus → sympathetic chain T10-L1 dorsal horn
- Poorly localised as large area of viscera supplied 

**Stage 2:**

- Full dilation to delivery of foetus  

**Pain mechanism** 

- Somatic pain from stretching and tearing of vagina  and perineum - well localised 
- Visceral pain from pressure on pelvis and pelvic structures  - poorly localised 

**Pain Pathways**

- Somatic pain transmission Adelta fibres from transmission along pudendal nerve (S2-4)

**Stage 3:**

-   After foetal delivery → delivery of placenta

**Pain mechanism** 

- Somatic pain from vagina  and perineum - well localised 
- Visceral pain from pelvic structures  - poorly localised 

**Pain Pathways**

- Somatic pain transmission Adelta fibres from transmission along pudendal nerve (S2-4)
